name: HOT PLATE
desc: Heavy-Duty Rectangular Laboratory Hot Plate engineered for uniform thermal heating and sample preparation workflows. Features a robust 12-inch heavy cast iron heating plate reaching surface temperatures up to 300°C.
principle: The INNOLAB INSTRUMENTS Hot Plate operates on the principle of electrical resistance heating. When electrical current passes through the internal heating element, electrical energy is converted into thermal energy, which is transferred to the cast iron heating plate and subsequently to the laboratory vessel through conductive heat transfer. The high thermal capacity of the plate supports consistent heating and helps maintain stable temperatures during routine chemical laboratory operations. In chemistry and analytical research laboratories, the hot plate is used for heating aqueous solutions, preparing reagents and buffers, warming reaction mixtures, concentrating non-volatile solutions, accelerating dissolution, and carrying out controlled heating during sample preparation. It is particularly useful in inorganic and analytical chemistry workflows involving the heating of suitable acid digestion mixtures, such as dilute mineral-acid preparations, for dissolving compatible solid samples before further analysis by techniques such as AAS or ICP-OES. Acid digestion must always be performed using chemically compatible vessels and an appropriate fume extraction system under an approved laboratory risk assessment. The hot plate can also support controlled heating during gravimetric analysis, crystallization, and other thermal preparation procedures. However, this conventional electrically heated model must not be assumed to be explosion-proof; direct heating of volatile or flammable organic solvents, including acetone, ethanol, methanol, and other VOC-containing mixtures, presents a fire and ignition hazard. Such procedures require an appropriately rated, ignition-protected heating arrangement selected through a documented risk assessment. The hot plate is therefore an important general-purpose heating instrument for chemical synthesis support, reagent preparation, analytical sample processing, and routine wet-laboratory applications.
sop: Place the hot plate on a stable, level, dry, and heat-resistant laboratory workbench. Ensure adequate clearance around the instrument and check that the heating surface, power cable, plug, and outer enclosure are free from visible damage.

Verify that the laboratory electrical supply matches the instrument's specified rating of 220 V, 50 Hz, and that the unit is connected to a properly earthed electrical outlet with suitable circuit protection.

Ensure the energy regulator is at its minimum or OFF position before switching on the instrument. Turn on the main electrical supply and the appropriate MCB, then switch on the hot plate. Confirm that the pilot lamp indicates the operating status.

Place a clean, dry, heat-resistant laboratory vessel containing the sample or solution centrally on the heating plate. Use an appropriate vessel such as a borosilicate glass beaker or compatible flask, and ensure that it is suitable for the intended temperature and chemical composition.

Gradually rotate the energy regulator clockwise to increase the heating output. Adjust the regulator incrementally according to the heating requirement of the experiment. This model uses an energy regulator; do not assume that it has a digital SET button or UP/DOWN controls.

Monitor the sample temperature using a suitable calibrated temperature-measuring device, where required. Allow sufficient time for the heating plate and sample to approach the desired working temperature, and wait for thermal stabilization before beginning temperature-sensitive experimental measurements.

During heating, observe the sample periodically. For solutions requiring uniform heating, use a chemically compatible stirring arrangement where appropriate. Avoid placing vessels with damaged bases or unstable shapes on the heating surface.

When the heating operation is complete, gradually reduce the energy regulator to its minimum or OFF position. Switch off the hot plate and then isolate the main electrical supply when the instrument is no longer required.

Allow the heating plate and vessel to cool naturally before handling, cleaning, or removing the equipment. Do not pour cold water onto the hot cast iron surface or use abrasive materials that may damage the heating plate.
Record the operating conditions, sample identification, heating duration, and any observations in the laboratory instrument logbook, as required by the laboratory's quality management procedure.

SAFETY WARNING: The heating plate and laboratory vessels can remain dangerously hot after switch-off. Use appropriate heat-resistant gloves and suitable personal protective equipment. Never touch the heating surface directly, leave the instrument unattended during operation, heat sealed containers, or directly heat volatile and flammable solvents on this conventional hot plate. Carry out approved acid-heating procedures in suitable fume extraction facilities using compatible vessels, and never operate the instrument if its electrical insulation, earthing, or power connection is damaged.
